title: Mining & metals
description: Ozone in gold and metal mining: ore pretreatment, leaching enhancement, cyanide destruction, and metal storage and surface cleaning. Eco-friendly technology for mineral processing and metalworking.

extraction-and-metals.title: Extraction and metals processing
extraction-and-metals.shortDesc: Ozone in gold mining: refractory ore pretreatment, leaching enhancement, cyanide destruction, and metal cleaning
extraction-and-metals.content:
Ozone is used in mining and metallurgy for pretreatment of refractory gold-bearing ores, heap leaching enhancement, cyanide destruction in wastewater, and metal surface cleaning. Industrial trials and deployment are underway in South Africa, Chile, Canada, and Southeast Asia.

Ozone pretreatment of refractory ores before cyanidation oxidizes sulfide minerals (pyrite, arsenopyrite), releasing gold and improving recovery from 53% to 88% (gold) and 26% to 78% (silver) in Mexican ore studies. Ozone is also used to destroy cyanide in tailings: 99% reduction of free and WAD cyanide at 2–3 g O₃ per gram CN.

goldRecovery.label: Gold recovery
goldRecovery.description: With ozone pretreatment of refractory ores

benefits: Higher gold and silver recovery from refractory ores
Cyanide destruction up to 99% without hazardous residues
Compliance with International Cyanide Management Code (ICMC)
Eco-friendly alternative to hypochlorite and peroxide

intro.paragraph1: Ozone (O₃) is a strong oxidant used in mining and metallurgy: pretreatment of refractory gold-bearing ores before cyanidation, heap leaching enhancement via oxygen supply, cyanide destruction in wastewater and tailings, and cleaning and passivation of metal surfaces during storage and processing.
intro.paragraph2: Industrial trials in South Africa, Chile, Canada, and Southeast Asia have demonstrated 85–99% reduction of free and WAD cyanide when using on-site ozone generation. The technology complies with the International Cyanide Management Code (ICMC) and allows reuse of treated water in the process.

dosage.title: Typical dosages:
dosage.text: Cyanide destruction: 2–3 g O₃ per gram CN (free and WAD). Thiocyanates: 3–4 g O₃ per gram SCN⁻. Refractory ore pretreatment: ozone concentration and contact time depend on ore type; full sulfide oxidation can reduce subsequent leaching time from 40 to 24 hours.

advantages.title: Advantages of ozone in mining and metallurgy
items: Oxidation of sulfide minerals in refractory ores — release of gold and silver
Heap leaching enhancement by increasing dissolved oxygen concentration
Complete cyanide destruction to cyanate, then bicarbonate and nitrogen
On-site ozone generation from air — no storage or transport of hazardous reagents
Cleaning and passivation of metal surfaces during storage and processing
Lower operating costs than hypochlorite at comparable effectiveness

refractoryOre.title: Ozone pretreatment of refractory ores
refractoryOre.intro: Refractory gold ores contain gold locked in sulfide minerals (pyrite, arsenopyrite, pyrrhotite), which limits recovery by conventional cyanidation. Ozone pretreatment oxidizes sulfides and improves gold and silver extraction.
refractoryOre.tableCaption: Results of ozone pretreatment of refractory ores (studies)
refractoryOre.note: Sulfide oxidation by ozone releases gold for subsequent cyanidation and can reduce cyanide consumption in the leaching stage.

cyanideDestruction.title: Cyanide destruction in wastewater
cyanideDestruction.intro: Ozone oxidizes free cyanide (CN⁻) to cyanate (CNO⁻), then with further oxidation and hydrolysis to bicarbonate and nitrogen. Typical reaction time 10–30 minutes. Industrial trials at gold operations in South Africa and Southeast Asia showed >99% reduction of free and WAD cyanide at 2–3 g O₃ per gram CN.

scheme.title: Ozone in the gold mining cycle

steps.title: Crushing and grinding
steps.description: Ore preparation for pretreatment or leaching

steps.title: Ozone pretreatment (refractory ores)
steps.description: Oxidation of sulfide minerals by ozone before cyanidation to improve gold and silver recovery

steps.title: Leaching (heap or tank)
steps.description: Cyanidation; in heap leaching, ozone or ozone ice can serve as an oxygen source to accelerate the process

steps.title: Cyanide destruction in tailings
steps.description: Ozonation of wastewater and slurry to destroy free and WAD cyanide to safe levels (ICMC)

steps.title: Water reuse
steps.description: Ozone-treated water can be returned to the process, reducing fresh water consumption

economic.title: Economics and deployment
economic.intro: Capital costs for ozone systems are higher than for some chemical oxidants, but operating costs are often lower (e.g. vs. sodium hypochlorite). The technology does not require tailings stream changes, provides fast and irreversible reaction, and improves operator safety by eliminating handling of hazardous chemicals.

benefits.title: Benefits of ozonation in mining and metallurgy

items.title: Higher recovery
items.description: Improved gold and silver recovery from refractory ores by 35–52% in studies

items.title: Cyanide safety
items.description: 99% destruction of free and WAD cyanide, compliance with international ICMC standards

items.title: Eco-friendly
items.description: Ozone decomposes to oxygen, leaves no toxic residues in water or tailings

items.title: Metal cleaning
items.description: Cleaning and passivation of metal surfaces during storage and processing without aggressive chemistry
